title: Events & RSVPs
callout: Answer in seconds, check in at the door

shots.say: Drills, meetings, training and fundraisers all live on the Events page. Here is how to find them, answer them, and check in.
Each card shows when the event is, where it is, and how many people are going.
Some drills carry the Counts toward attendance badge, beside Mandatory. Your department grades a training requirement on how many of these you attend, so turning up is what counts.
Switch to the calendar to see the month at a glance, then back to the list.
Open an event for the full details, then press RSVP Now.
Choose Going or Not Going. Some events also offer Maybe. You can add a note, then submit.
Done. Your officers can see you're coming, and you can change your answer until the RSVP deadline.
Once the deadline passes, or the event ends, the RSVP button goes away. Missed it? Check in when you get there.
Some events have a limit on how many can go. When every spot is taken, the event shows as full.
Answering Going then puts you on the waitlist, and your RSVP shows your place in line.
If a spot opens up, you're moved to Going automatically. You'll get a notification in the app, and an email too, unless you've turned that email off.
At the event, an officer puts up a check-in code by the door.
Scan it with your phone's camera, and the event's check-in page opens. Press Check In to This Event.
You're checked in. No paper sign-in sheet, and no line.
Your arrival time is recorded exactly as it happened. Arrive long before the start, and your credit still counts from the scheduled start time.
If an event is over and you never got checked in, open it and press I was there.
Say why there's no check-in, and when you arrived and left if you know. The organizer is told, and confirms or declines your request.
While it's waiting, you can withdraw it and send a corrected one. You can ask for up to thirty days after the event.
To look back, switch Events to Past. A mandatory event with no check-in on record is marked, so you can see what still needs sorting out.
That's events. Next, your training and certifications.
